purposes.pods: Runs one or more containers together with shared networking and volumes.
purposes.apps/deployments: Declares the desired application version and replica count; manages ReplicaSets during updates.
purposes.apps/replicasets: Maintains the desired number of matching Pods; normally managed by a Deployment.
purposes.apps/statefulsets: Manages Pods with stable identities and persistent-storage associations.
purposes.apps/daemonsets: Runs a Pod on each eligible Node, often for node-level agents.
purposes.batch/jobs: Runs a finite task and tracks successful Pod completions.
purposes.batch/cronjobs: Creates Jobs according to a schedule.
purposes.replicationcontrollers: Legacy controller that maintains a desired Pod count; prefer Deployment for new workloads.
purposes.services: Provides a stable network endpoint for a set of backends, commonly selected Pods.
purposes.endpoints: Legacy list of Service backend addresses; EndpointSlice is the modern replacement.
purposes.discovery.k8s.io/endpointslices: Stores a bounded slice of backend addresses and readiness for a Service.
purposes.networking.k8s.io/ingresses: Declares HTTP/HTTPS routing to Services; requires an Ingress controller.
purposes.networking.k8s.io/ingressclasses: Identifies the controller and parameters used for an Ingress class.
purposes.networking.k8s.io/networkpolicies: Declares allowed ingress and egress for selected Pods; enforcement needs a supporting network plugin.
purposes.secrets: Stores sensitive data referenced by workloads; base64 is encoding, not encryption.
purposes.nodes: Represents a machine that can run Pods, with capacity and health conditions.
purposes.namespaces: Scopes names and many policies within a cluster; it is not a separate cluster.
purposes.events: Reports an observation by a component about an object; retention is limited.
purposes.autoscaling/horizontalpodautoscalers: Adjusts a workload replica count using configured metrics and bounds.
purposes.resourcequotas: Limits aggregate resource consumption or object counts in a Namespace.
purposes.limitranges: Defines defaults and constraints for resource requests and limits within a Namespace.
purposes.policy/poddisruptionbudgets: Limits concurrent voluntary disruptions of selected Pods through eviction.
purposes.scheduling.k8s.io/priorityclasses: Defines scheduling priority and preemption behavior for Pods.
purposes.node.k8s.io/runtimeclasses: Selects a container runtime configuration for Pods.
purposes.coordination.k8s.io/leases: Coordinates heartbeats or leader election through renewable ownership records.
purposes.admissionregistration.k8s.io/mutatingweb: Registers webhooks that can modify matching API requests before admission.
purposes.admissionregistration.k8s.io/validatingw: Registers webhooks that accept or reject matching API requests without modifying them.
purposes.apiextensions.k8s.io/customresourcedefin: Defines a custom API resource type; a separate controller may implement its behavior.
purposes.persistentvolumeclaims: Requests persistent storage and binds to a suitable PersistentVolume.
purposes.persistentvolumes: Represents a provisioned storage resource with a reclaim policy.
purposes.storage.k8s.io/storageclasses: Defines a storage provisioner and parameters for dynamic volume provisioning.
purposes.serviceaccounts: Provides an identity for processes in Pods when accessing the Kubernetes API.
purposes.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/roles: Defines permitted API actions within a Namespace; requires a binding to grant them.
purposes.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/rolebindings: Grants a Role or ClusterRole to subjects within one Namespace.
purposes.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/clusterroles: Defines reusable API permissions, including cluster-scoped resources.
purposes.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/clusterrolebin: Grants a ClusterRole to subjects across the cluster.

ui.lesson: Why did the Pod come back?
ui.isolation: No cluster, account or kubeconfig is used. Actions affect only this lesson. Scheduling, networking and real controller timing are not simulated.
ui.intro: Inspect the application, remove one simulated Pod, then find what restored it. Start by opening any row and following its relationships.
ui.deleted: The Pod is gone. Desired replicas: 2; observed Pods: 1. Advance the controller to observe reconciliation.
ui.replaced: A new Pod with a new UID now exists. The desired count stayed 2. Inspect its owner relationships, events and logs.
ui.hintText: Follow metadata.ownerReferences: Pod → ReplicaSet → Deployment. ReplicaSet restores the desired count; Deployment manages ReplicaSets and rollouts.
ui.challenge: The application now has unfamiliar names. Open the Pod and navigate to its Deployment through owner relationships. Then explain why a replacement appeared.
ui.question: Why was a new Pod created?
ui.answerController: The ReplicaSet reconciled the actual Pod count with its desired replicas.
ui.answerRestart: The deleted Pod restarted itself with the same identity.
ui.answerService: The Service created another Pod to restore its backends.
ui.retry: That does not explain controller reconciliation. Inspect the owner chain and try again.
ui.findOwner: First navigate from the new Pod to its owning Deployment. Concept links in help are not object ownership evidence.
ui.complete: You found the owner chain and explained reconciliation without hints in the check.
ui.noLogs: Only the application Pods have logs in this lesson.
ui.select: Select a row to inspect it.

cautions.workload: Desired state is not readiness. Deleting a controlled Pod does not change the desired count; its controller may create a new Pod with a different UID. Container restart and Pod replacement are different.
cautions.network: A routing declaration does not prove reachability or create application Pods. Check selectors, ports, ready endpoints and the relevant controller or data plane.
cautions.policy: Selection is not proof of enforcement. NetworkPolicy requires a supporting plugin; allowed rules combine additively, and both ingress and egress isolation can matter.
cautions.config: Changing configuration does not necessarily restart Pods. Environment variables need a new container; mounted updates and application reload behavior differ.
cautions.secret: A Secret is not automatically encrypted at rest. Access control, encryption configuration and application handling still matter. This help never reads Secret values.
cautions.node: Declared capacity or runtime settings do not guarantee a Pod can run. Eligibility, allocatable resources, taints and current conditions also matter.
cautions.namespace: A Namespace alone is not a security or network boundary. RBAC, policies and cluster-scoped resources need separate consideration.
cautions.event: Events are observations, not a complete audit log. Repeated events can be aggregated; missing or expired events do not prove that nothing happened.
cautions.capacity: A configured number is not guaranteed capacity. Limits, defaults, quotas, metrics availability and scheduling constraints serve different purposes; inspect the relevant status.
cautions.disruption: A PDB is not a general availability guarantee. It constrains supported voluntary evictions, not direct Pod deletion or every failure and controller rollout.
cautions.lease: A Lease is a coordination record, not proof that a holder is healthy or exclusive in every failure mode. Check timing and the using component.
cautions.admission: A registered webhook is not proof of successful enforcement. Matching rules, service reachability, certificates, failurePolicy and side effects matter.
cautions.extension: A CRD defines an API and schema, not an installed operator’s behavior. Custom schema descriptions may be unreviewed or untranslated; consult the operator’s documentation.
cautions.storage: A claim or volume is not a backup or an availability guarantee. Binding, access modes, topology and reclaim policy affect use and data retention.
cautions.access: Identity is not permission. Roles need bindings; RoleBinding is namespace-scoped even when it references a ClusterRole. Declared rules alone do not prove an actual request is authorized.
